title: Communicating an incident: during, after and to whom

videos.script: Friday, 19:09, Marola's busiest hour. Checkout stops working for almost everybody. {{title}} For the next half hour, the people fixing it should not also be the people explaining it. So the first thing is roles: one person in command, one fixing, one talking, one writing it down. {{roles}} Then the updates. What is affected, what is being done, and when the next update comes. And it comes when it said it would, even if nothing has changed. {{timeline}} Five audiences hear about it, each in a different way. Support needs a sentence to say to the next customer more than any explanation. {{fanout}} Then the summary the next morning, the letter to customers, and the words that cause trouble when they are written in a hurry.
